preference.statement: Write the model down before writing code: every decision-variable family, the objective sense, and every constraint family must be stated explicitly in a reviewable specification.
preference.rationale: A formulation that exists only inside code cannot be reviewed by an analyst before the solve; omissions hide there.

required: Before the program, return a JSON specification block with problem_type, decision_variables (name, domain, bounds, meaning), objective (sense, expression), constraints (name, expression, which sentence of the problem it comes from), and assumptions.
checks: the JSON spec exists and lists decision variables, an objective sense, and at least one constraint

repair.instruction: Return the specification as valid JSON in its own ```json block, closed with ``` before the program starts (write null, true and false, never None, True or False; separate list items with commas), and make it list decision_variables, objective.sense and constraints so that it describes the model implemented in the program.

audit.note: Seed rule; not derived from benchmark failures. | 1.0.1 (packet_it0 proposal M6): repair instruction names the JSON syntax errors behind every spec failure on dev (15 C2 outputs: 9 x Python None instead of null, 4 x JSON cut off by a closing fence in mid-string, 2 x missing comma between list items). Predicate and firings unchanged.

preference.statement: The deliverable is an executable program, not prose: the answer must contain one complete Python program using pulp.
preference.rationale: Only an executable program can be checked against the solver.

required: Return exactly one complete, runnable Python program in a ```python block that builds the model with pulp, solves it, and prints the required STATUS and FINAL_OBJECTIVE lines.
forbidden: Do not leave placeholders, pseudo-code, or TODO comments in the program.
checks: a runnable pulp program is present

repair.instruction: Return the complete Python program in a ```python block.

audit.note: Seed rule.

preference.statement: Preserve the objective direction stated in the problem: the spec's objective sense and the program's LpMinimize/LpMaximize must agree with each other and with the text.
preference.rationale: A reversed objective sense produces a confidently wrong optimum; it is one of the most common and least visible formulation errors.

required: State the objective sense (minimize or maximize) in the spec and use the matching pulp sense constant in the program.
forbidden: Do not maximize a cost or minimize a profit.
checks: objective sense in the spec matches LpMinimize/LpMaximize in the program

repair.instruction: Make the objective sense in the spec and the pulp sense constant in the program agree with the problem statement.

audit.note: Seed rule. | 1.1.0 (packet_it0 proposal M7): predicate v2: not applicable when the spec is missing or unparseable (orgene.artifact.spec_present reports it); a program without a sense constant is read as LpMinimize, PuLP's default. packet_it0 dev C2 signal55: v1 fails on the 10 outputs whose spec does not parse (3 of them correct), always together with spec_present; v2 fails on none of them (constraints v2 still fails mamo_complex_lp-0108 C2, a truncated program without constraints).

preference.statement: Declare the domain of every decision variable (continuous, integer, or binary) in the spec and implement the same domain in the program.
preference.rationale: Silently relaxing integer or binary variables changes the problem and its optimum.

required: Give every decision variable a domain in the spec, and declare the same category (Continuous, Integer, Binary) with pulp cat=... in the program.
forbidden: Do not relax integer or binary requirements without saying so in assumptions.
checks: integer/binary domains in the spec are declared in the program

repair.instruction: Declare the integer/binary variables in the program with cat='Integer' or cat='Binary' exactly as the spec states.

audit.note: Seed rule. | 1.1.0 (packet_it0 proposal M7): predicate v2: not applicable when the spec is missing or unparseable (orgene.artifact.spec_present reports it). packet_it0 dev C2 signal55: v1 fails on the 10 outputs whose spec does not parse (3 of them correct), always together with spec_present; v2 fails on none of them (constraints v2 still fails mamo_complex_lp-0108 C2, a truncated program without constraints).

preference.statement: Every requirement sentence in the problem becomes a named constraint family in the spec, and every spec constraint is added to the program.
preference.rationale: Missing constraints are the dominant failure mode of LLM formulations; naming each constraint after its source sentence makes omissions visible.

required: List each constraint in the spec with the sentence it comes from, and add each one to the pulp problem with a name.
forbidden: Do not merge unrelated requirements into one constraint; do not drop a requirement because it looks redundant.
checks: the spec lists constraints and the program adds constraints

repair.instruction: Add every constraint from the spec to the program (prob += ...) and make sure the spec lists every requirement stated in the problem.

audit.note: Seed rule. | 1.1.0 (packet_it0 proposal M7): predicate v2: not applicable when the spec is missing or unparseable; program constraints counted from the AST (any problem-object name). packet_it0 dev C2 signal55: v1 fails on the 10 outputs whose spec does not parse (3 of them correct), always together with spec_present; v2 fails on none of them (constraints v2 still fails mamo_complex_lp-0108 C2, a truncated program without constraints).

preference.statement: Report only what the solver computed: the objective value must come from the solver after solve(), never from a number typed into the program.
preference.rationale: A printed constant is not a solution; it is an unsupported claim dressed as output.

required: Call prob.solve(...) and print FINAL_OBJECTIVE from pulp.value(prob.objective).
forbidden: Do not hard-code the objective value or decision values; do not print FINAL_OBJECTIVE before solving.
checks: solve() is called before FINAL_OBJECTIVE is printed and the value comes from the solver

repair.instruction: Solve the model with prob.solve(pulp.PULP_CBC_CMD(msg=0)) and print FINAL_OBJECTIVE from pulp.value(prob.objective).

audit.note: Seed rule; descends from the v2 solver-evidence boundary gene.

preference.statement: Always expose the solver status next to the objective value.
preference.rationale: An objective value without its status hides infeasible, unbounded, or not-solved outcomes.

required: Print STATUS: followed by pulp.LpStatus[prob.status] before FINAL_OBJECTIVE.
checks: solver status is printed

repair.instruction: Print the line STATUS: <pulp.LpStatus[prob.status]> before FINAL_OBJECTIVE.

audit.note: Seed rule.

preference.statement: A model that does not run is not a model: the program must execute without error and report both lines.
preference.rationale: Runtime failures are cheap to detect and repair, and they mask every other quality signal.

required: Use only the standard library and pulp; define every symbol you use; keep index sets consistent.
checks: the program runs to completion within the time limit and prints STATUS and FINAL_OBJECTIVE

repair.instruction: Fix the runtime error shown in stderr without changing the model's meaning; keep the same variables, objective, and constraints unless the error is in them.

audit.note: Seed rule.

preference.statement: Treat an infeasible or unbounded status as a formulation defect until proven otherwise: re-check constraint directions, bounds, and data before accepting it.
preference.rationale: Benchmark instances are almost always feasible and bounded; these statuses usually signal a reversed inequality, a wrong bound, or a misread number.

required: If the solver reports Infeasible or Unbounded, re-check every inequality direction, every bound, and every number against the text; if the instance is truly infeasible or unbounded, say so in assumptions.
forbidden: Do not report a numeric objective when the status is not Optimal.
checks: the final status is Optimal, or the non-optimal status is justified in assumptions

repair.instruction: Re-derive the constraints that could make the model infeasible or unbounded (inequality directions, equalities that should be inequalities, bounds, variables left without a lower bound, missing capacity or demand limits) and correct the ones that the re-derivation shows to be wrong; keep the others unchanged.

audit.note: Seed rule. | 1.0.1 (packet_it0 proposal M4): repair instruction no longer refers to spec assumptions (C3L answers have no spec; the C3 contract still asks for the assumption); adds two common causes (an equality where the text states a bound, and PuLP's default lower bound of minus infinity). Predicate and firings unchanged.

preference.statement: Every number in the program must come from the problem text or be a stated derivation of one; never invent a coefficient, capacity, demand, or cost.
preference.rationale: Hallucinated data produces a plausible model of a different problem.

required: Take every coefficient and bound from the problem statement; if a value must be derived (unit conversion, total), show the derivation in the spec assumptions.
forbidden: Do not invent missing data; if something is missing, state the assumption explicitly.
checks: numeric literals in the program are traceable to the problem text (warning only)

repair.instruction: Verify each flagged number against the text; correct misread values, and keep numbers that are derived from the text (unit conversions, totals) with a short comment saying how they were derived.

audit.note: Seed rule; soft because unit conversions legitimately introduce new literals. | 1.1.0 (packet_it0 proposal M5): predicate v2 reads sentence-final numbers and number words in the text, reads only real numeric literals in the program (not comments or strings), skips range()/subscript indices and allows unit-conversion factors; instruction no longer refers to spec assumptions. packet_it0 dev signal55: v1 fails 11 wrong / 14 correct on C0 and 11 / 7 on C2; v2 fails 3 / 1 on C0 and 0 / 0 on C2. Stays soft.

preference.statement: Derive big-M constants from the data (capacities, total demand) instead of using arbitrary huge numbers.
preference.rationale: Loose big-M values weaken relaxations and cause numerical trouble; they also hide the logic they are supposed to encode.

required: When a big-M linking constraint is needed, set M to a bound derived from the problem data and name it.
forbidden: Do not use arbitrary constants like 1e6 or 999999 as big-M.
checks: no arbitrary very large constants appear in the program (warning only)

repair.instruction: Replace the arbitrary large constant with a bound derived from the data (e.g. total demand or capacity).

audit.note: Seed rule; descends from the v1 lot-sizing big-M atom.

preference.statement: A mapping whose keys are tuples must be read with a tuple key, d[i, j]; d[i][j] looks up d[i] and fails.
preference.rationale: pulp.LpVariable.dicts over a generator of tuples, and dict comprehensions with tuple keys, produce a flat mapping keyed by the tuple. Writing d[i][j] is the single most common way a correct formulation dies at run time.

required: Read a tuple-keyed mapping as d[i, j]; read a nested mapping as d[i][j]. Pick one shape and use it everywhere.
forbidden: Do not mix the two shapes: never index a tuple-keyed mapping (from LpVariable.dicts over tuples, or {(i, j): ...}) with two separate subscripts.
checks: tuple-keyed mappings are indexed with a tuple key, not two subscripts

repair.instruction: Index the flagged mapping with a tuple key, d[i, j], everywhere it is read, or build it as a nested mapping instead. Keep the rest of the model unchanged.

audit.note: dev C0: 8 cases died with KeyError on the first subscript. Predicate precision 1.00 on dev C0 (9/9 firings on wrong answers) and 1.00 on dev C2.

preference.statement: A mapping built on a subset of index pairs must be read only on the keys it actually has.
preference.rationale: Cost and capacity tables are routinely built only for the pairs that exist, then read over the full Cartesian product; the missing key raises at run time. Excluding the diagonal counts as dense and needs no membership test.

required: Iterate the mapping's own keys, or guard every read with `if (i, j) in mapping`, whenever the mapping was built on a subset of pairs.
forbidden: Do not read a sparsely built mapping over the full product of its index sets.
checks: reads of sparsely built mappings are restricted to the keys those mappings have

repair.instruction: Restrict every read of the flagged mapping to the pairs it defines: iterate its keys, or add an `if (i, j) in <mapping>` guard to the comprehension.

audit.note: dev C0: 5 cases. Predicate distinguishes 'full product minus diagonal' (an `i != j` guard suffices) from arbitrary sparsity (needs membership); precision 1.00 on dev C0 and C2. | 1.1.0 (packet_it0 proposal M8): predicate v2 runs after execution and reports v1's static finding only when the program did not run cleanly; v1 does not recognise a guard by membership in the table the mapping was built from, nor an off-diagonal read written against a fixed index, and a program that ran to the end cannot have hit a missing key. packet_it0 dev: v1 fails on two programs that ran to completion (signal55 C0 mamo_complex_lp-0105, wrong only because of its single-arc objective; types_only C0 mamo_complex_lp-0114); v2 keeps every firing on a program that stopped with KeyError (signal55 C2 mamo_complex_lp-0101; types_only C0 mamo_complex_lp-0048, -0116, -0130, -0147) and drops those two.

preference.statement: Use only attributes that PuLP actually provides.
preference.rationale: When a formulation needs something PuLP cannot express, the model tends to invent an API for it rather than reformulate; the invented call is both a run-time error and a sign that the formulation is not linear.

required: Build the model with the documented PuLP API: LpProblem, LpVariable, lpSum, lpDot, LpConstraint, value, and the solver classes.
forbidden: Do not call PuLP helpers that do not exist (there is no product, norm, or mathematical-constant helper); reformulate instead.
checks: every pulp.<attribute> used in the program is a real PuLP attribute

repair.instruction: Remove the non-existent PuLP call and express the same requirement with linear PuLP constructs (LpVariable, lpSum, lpDot, constraints added with +=). If the quantity is genuinely non-linear, linearize it exactly (one variable per tier, one 0/1 variable per allowed value or combination, indicator binaries), and make sure FINAL_OBJECTIVE still reports the value of the objective the question asks for. Keep the rest of the model unchanged.

audit.note: dev C0 2 cases (pulp.pi, pulp.lpNorm, pulp.lpProduct) + dev C2 1 further case. Precision 1.00 on both. | 1.1.0 (packet_it0 proposal M3): repair instruction no longer refers to spec assumptions (C3L answers have no spec) and warns that a transformed objective must still be reported in the original units; params.extra_allowed adds names documented on the PuLP constants and solvers pages (coin-or.github.io/pulp, read 2026-09-29) plus the four LpStatus* constants of the pulp 2.x constants module (to be checked against the installed PuLP). packet_it0 dev: no change in firings (industryor-0099 C0, mamo_complex_lp-0108 C2, mamo_complex_lp-0197 C0/C2).

preference.statement: Decision variables may appear only in linear expressions: no min/max/abs/round applied to them, no variable times variable, no division by a variable, no %, // or ** on a variable, no data table indexed by a variable, no Python if on a variable, no comparison used as an arithmetic term.
preference.rationale: Ratio requirements, tiered prices, implications and products are the four places a linear formulation silently becomes non-linear. Each has a standard linear encoding, and reaching for the arithmetic shortcut is what fails.

required: Cross-multiply ratio requirements; give each price or quantity tier its own variable with its own bounds; encode implications with indicator binaries and a big-M derived from the data.
forbidden: Do not apply min(), max(), abs() or round() to an expression containing a decision variable; do not multiply or divide two expressions that both contain decision variables; do not use a comparison as a term.
Do not index a data table with a decision variable, do not apply %, // or ** to a decision variable, and do not test a decision variable with a Python if.
checks: every expression containing a decision variable is linear

repair.instruction: Rewrite the flagged expression linearly: cross-multiply a ratio; split a tiered quantity into one variable per tier with ordering binaries; replace a table lookup or any function of a discrete choice by one 0/1 variable per allowed value (exactly one of them equal to 1); write 'a multiple of k' as x == k * n with an integer variable n; replace a Python if or a comparison on a variable by an indicator binary with a big-M taken from the data bounds. Keep the rest of the model unchanged.

audit.note: dev C0 4 cases. One firing on a correct answer (industryor-0019: `10 * (x_B >= 10)`) is a real defect that happened not to move the optimum, so precision 0.80 understates it. | 1.1.0 (packet_it0 proposals M2): predicate v2 adds %, //, **, data-table-indexed-by-a-variable and if-tests on variables; repair instruction no longer refers to spec assumptions (C3L answers have no spec). packet_it0 dev: new firings industryor-0025 C2 (x % 2) and industryor-0099 C0 (table indexed by a variable; that output is also failed by orgene.code.pulp_api_exists); no new firing on a correct answer (industryor-0019 C0 as in v1).

preference.statement: When the goal is a total, the objective must aggregate over the whole index set, not name a single element of a variable family.
preference.rationale: A throughput or total-cost objective written as one indexed variable optimises that element alone and silently returns its bound. The constraints already range over the index set, so the mismatch is visible in the program.

required: Write an aggregate objective as an lpSum over the relevant index set; for a network throughput this is the net flow out of the source, not the capacity of one arc.
forbidden: Do not set the objective to a single element of a variable family whose other elements the constraints range over.
checks: the objective aggregates the whole declared variable family rather than naming one element

repair.instruction: The objective must aggregate over the whole declared variable family, not name a single element of it. Replace the single-element objective with the total the question asks for: an lpSum over the relevant index set (for a network throughput, the net flow out of the source, i.e. the sum of the arcs leaving it minus the sum of the arcs entering it). Leave the constraints unchanged.

audit.note: dev C0: 8 cases, six of them max-flow programs that returned the capacity of the single arc they optimised. Promoted from soft to hard on 2026-09-06 (approved by the author): precision was 1.00 over 170 dev observations (85 cases x dev C0 and dev C2) with zero firings on a correct answer, and as a soft gene it would not have driven a repair on the four max-flow cases that carry no hard failure of their own.

preference.statement: A binary counted in a cardinality constraint must also bound the quantity it switches.
preference.rationale: Writing `sum(b) <= k` without `quantity <= M * b` leaves the count with nothing to count: the quantity stays positive while its indicator is zero, and the restriction has no effect on the optimum. When every decision variable is binary the binaries are the decisions themselves (selection, covering, assignment) and there is nothing to link; the check applies only when the program also has quantities.

required: Link every indicator binary to its quantity in both directions that the requirement needs, with a big-M taken from the data bounds.
forbidden: Do not rely on a cardinality constraint over binaries that are not linked to the quantities they are supposed to switch on and off.
checks: binaries appearing in cardinality constraints are linked to the quantities they switch

repair.instruction: For every flagged binary b, add the link `quantity <= M * b` to the quantity that b stands for, with M the largest value that quantity can take (a capacity, a demand or a total from the data), and `quantity >= m * b` when the requirement also implies a positive minimum. Keep the rest of the model unchanged.

audit.note: dev C0 2 cases + dev C2 1 case. Soft: precision 1.00 on dev C0 but 0.50 on dev C2 (one firing on a correct answer). | 1.1.0 (packet_it0 proposal M1): predicate v2 exempts all-binary programs; severity soft -> hard. packet_it0 dev: v2 fails on signal55 C0 industryor-0049, industryor-0058 and C2 industryor-0049, all wrong and all without any other hard failure; the three firings of v1 on correct answers (industryor-0053 C0/C2, industryor-0010 C2, all-binary selection or covering models) disappear. v1.0.0 cited industryor-0077 and mamo_complex_lp-0094, whose programs are all-binary, so v2 no longer fires on them.

preference.statement: Treat an optimal objective value of zero as a formulation defect until shown otherwise: a model that is optimal by doing nothing, or by a trivial assignment, has usually lost a requirement or measures the wrong quantity.
preference.rationale: Validating a model does not stop at an Optimal status; the solution must be plausible for the problem it claims to solve (Williams 2013, sec. 6.1; Gass 1983). A stated optimisation problem almost never has a zero optimum: a zero means nothing is produced, shipped, assigned or visited, which happens when a covering, demand or assignment requirement was dropped, when a variable can take a meaningless value such as assigning an item to itself, or when the objective counts a quantity the solver can drive to zero.

required: Before reporting, check that the optimal solution is plausible: every requirement that forces activity (demands met, items assigned or placed, locations visited, required totals reached) is in the model, and the objective is the quantity the question asks for.
forbidden: Do not accept an optimal objective of 0 without checking that doing nothing really satisfies every requirement of the problem.
checks: an optimal objective value of 0 is flagged for re-checking

repair.instruction: Find what lets the model reach 0 and correct it: add any requirement from the text that forces activity (every demand met, every item assigned or placed, every location visited, a required total reached), exclude meaningless variables such as an item assigned to itself, and make sure the objective is the quantity the question asks for (when it asks to minimise the largest of several totals, minimise an auxiliary variable that is at least every one of those totals). If zero really is the optimum of the problem as stated, return the program unchanged.

audit.note: packet_it0 dev: signal55 C0 industryor-0081 and mamo_complex_lp-0087, C2 industryor-0058 (all judged wrong); types_only C0 mamo_complex_lp-0097 (self-assignments allowed at zero cost: wrong from the program alone). No firing on a correct signal55 answer.

activation.rationale: A zero optimum is a property of the solution, not of the problem wording; no text feature predicts it, so the check runs on every problem.

preference.statement: A logical condition between decisions (if one option is taken another must or must not be, not both, at most k of them) is written with 0/1 indicator variables linked to the quantities, never directly on the quantities.
preference.rationale: Implications, exclusions and counts of used options are not linear conditions on the quantities; the standard encoding introduces a 0/1 variable per decision, links it to its quantity with a data-derived bound, and states the logic on the 0/1 variables (Williams 2013, ch. 9). Without them the condition is dropped, turned into an unconditional bound, or written as a meaningless inequality on quantities such as a + b <= 1.

required: Model every if-then, not-both or at-most-k-of condition between decisions with 0/1 indicator variables: link each indicator to its quantity (x <= M*y with M taken from the data, and x >= m*y when a minimum applies) and state the condition on the indicators (y_a <= y_b, y_a + y_b <= 1, sum of y <= k).
forbidden: Do not write a logical condition on the quantities themselves (such as a + b <= 1 or a + b == 0 for 'not both') and do not replace a conditional requirement by an unconditional one.
checks: problems that state logical conditions between decisions declare 0/1 indicator variables

repair.instruction: For each conditional or exclusive requirement, add a 0/1 indicator for each decision it mentions (e.g. 'option j is used'), link it to the quantity with x_j <= M*y_j (and x_j >= m*y_j when a minimum amount is implied), taking M from the data (a capacity, a demand or the largest value x_j can take), and write the logic on the indicators: 'if A then B' as y_A <= y_B, 'if A then not B' or 'not both' as y_A + y_B <= 1, 'at most k of them' as the sum of the y's <= k. Remove any constraint that wrote the condition directly on the quantities. Keep the rest of the model unchanged.

audit.note: packet_it0 dev: signal55 C0 industryor-0009, industryor-0024 (wrong); C2 industryor-0009, industryor-0019, industryor-0024, industryor-0058 (wrong). One firing on a correct answer: industryor-0019 C0, whose logic is written as a comparison used as a term (already failed by orgene.model.linear_expressions_only, so the gene adds no new repair there).

activation.rationale: The gene has something to check only when the text states a logical condition between decisions; the draft lexicon's logical_terms contains the predicate's own cue patterns, so the rule is never false where the predicate can fail.

preference.statement: Every constraint must be satisfiable on its own and must leave its variables room to be positive: with non-negative variables entering with one sign, a right-hand side that leaves no room is a sign or direction error.
preference.rationale: A single row that no non-negative point satisfies is the smallest irreducible infeasible subsystem (Chinneck 2008, part II), and a row that forces a sum of non-negative variables to zero fixes all of them at zero, so the variables it mentions are pointless. Both are what a reviewer finds first when reading constraint signs (Williams 2013, sec. 6.1 on infeasible models): a reversed inequality, a term on the wrong side, a constant with the wrong sign, or a logical condition such as 'not both' written on the quantities.

required: Write each constraint with the direction and signs the text states; with non-negative variables, check that each constraint can hold with some of its variables positive.
forbidden: Do not write a constraint that forces a sum of non-negative variables to be at most or equal to 0, or to be at most a negative number, unless the text says those quantities must all be zero.
checks: no single constraint is infeasible on its own or forces all of its variables to zero

repair.instruction: Re-derive each flagged constraint from its sentence in the problem: check the direction (<=, >=, ==), the side each term belongs on, and the sign of the constant; a quantity the text says is used, required or produced must be able to be positive. If the constraint was meant to express a logical condition (either/or, not both, if-then), remove it and model the condition with 0/1 indicator variables linked to the quantities. Keep the other constraints unchanged.

audit.note: packet_it0 dev: signal55 C0 industryor-0024 (a + b == 0 for 'not both'), industryor-0040 (four rows with a positive constant bounded by 0; solver Infeasible), C2 industryor-0009, industryor-0058 (all wrong). No firing on a correct answer; rows with data-dependent coefficients are not analysed.

activation.rationale: A sign error can occur in any model; the check is structural and cheap, so it runs on every problem.

preference.statement: Quantities that count indivisible units are integer variables; a continuous relaxation is acceptable only when the text allows fractional amounts or the quantities are divisible.
preference.rationale: Indivisibility is the first reason for integer variables, and rounding a fractional LP optimum is not a valid substitute (Williams 2013, ch. 8 and sec. 9.1). With integer data and an all-continuous model, a fractional optimum proves that some decisions are fractional; whether that is allowed depends on what the decisions count, which the model has to decide from the text.

required: Declare a decision variable Integer when it counts indivisible units (items, servings, vehicles, people, trips, whole batches) unless the text states that fractional amounts are allowed; keep it Continuous for divisible amounts (weight, volume, time, money, area).
forbidden: Do not relax an integer requirement silently; if you model a count as continuous, say why in the spec assumptions.
checks: an all-continuous model with integer objective data and a fractional optimum is flagged when the text does not allow fractional amounts

repair.instruction: Decide for each decision variable whether it counts indivisible units (items, servings, vehicles, people, trips, whole batches). Declare those with cat='Integer' in the program and domain 'integer' in the spec; keep divisible amounts (weights, volumes, hours, money, area) continuous. If every quantity is genuinely divisible, return the answer unchanged.

audit.note: packet_it0 dev C2 only (C0 programs of the same cases declare integers and are judged correct on five of them): seven signal55 firings, all on wrong answers; types_only C2 mamo_complex_lp-0018, -0023, -0208 also fire (correctness unknown, not counted). Scoped to C3 because C0 outputs show no such error; evaluated on C0 it would fire once, on industryor-0032 (judged correct within the 1e-4 tolerance, LP optimum just above the integral reference).

activation.rationale: When the text says fractional amounts are allowed, a fractional optimum is intended; the rule and the predicate use the same wording pattern.
